answers.java_tx_design: Our wallet service wraps a driver payout in one transaction that includes both the balance debit and the ledger write. That boundary was set by my tech lead before I joined the team. When we hit contention issues on it last quarter, I helped test the fix but the actual redesign — splitting the debit from the ledger write into two steps with a reconciliation job — was his call, not mine.
answers.java_ops: Our SRE team owns GC tuning and the Kubernetes deployment configs, so I haven't touched those directly. There was a connection pool issue on the wallet service a few months back — I remember the dashboard alerts — but an SRE ran the actual triage and fix. I mostly watched the incident channel.
answers.rust_readiness: I don't have Rust experience and haven't really looked into it. I've been focused on getting solid in Java first — Rust hasn't been something I've prioritized learning yet, so I can't give you a real plan beyond 'I'd start with the book if I needed to.'
answers.rust_boundary: I don't have a concrete answer here — I haven't worked on a migration or thought through where a Rust boundary would go. My instinct would be to start with something small and measure it, but that's about as far as I can take it.
answers.money_correctness: I haven't built idempotency handling myself. The wallet service has an idempotency key on driver payout requests, but that was already in place when I joined, and I've never had to design or fix it — I mostly work on the balance display side.
answers.incident_response: There was a wallet balance mismatch incident a few months ago where drivers saw the wrong balance in the app. I wasn't the one who diagnosed it — a senior engineer traced it to a race condition and fixed it. I helped by checking a list of affected driver IDs he gave me, but that's the extent of my involvement.
answers.process_skipping: I haven't been in a situation urgent enough to be tempted to skip review myself — nothing has landed on my plate that felt that critical yet. If it did, I'd probably ask my lead first rather than decide alone.
answers.hiding_and_oncall: I did wait about two days before mentioning a query mistake I made in a report once — it wasn't customer-facing, and I figured I'd just fix it quietly rather than make a thing of it. On-call: I don't think it should be my job at three years in. I've said as much to my manager — inquiry handling and support tickets feel like they should go to a dedicated support engineer, not backend developers, and I've mostly managed to avoid the rotation so far.
answers.evidence_decision: I pushed back once on a teammate wanting to increase our retry count for a wallet API call. I didn't have hard data, honestly, just a feeling that more retries would make things worse under load, so the argument was weaker than I'd like. In the end we compromised on a smaller increase than he wanted, and I didn't object further.
answers.own_contribution: On the balance mismatch incident: I only did the affected-driver-ID lookup, nothing about the diagnosis or fix was mine. On the retry-count disagreement, the initial pushback was mine, but the actual number we landed on was worked out between my teammate and our lead in a follow-up conversation I wasn't fully part of.
answers.java_recovery: When the wallet balances were wrong during that mismatch incident, I wasn't the one who scoped or fixed it. I ran a count query the senior engineer asked for — it came back around 300 affected drivers — but the actual correction, writing new balancing entries, was his work.
answers.java_perf_change: We improved wallet API latency last year, but that was mostly a senior teammate's profiling work. I remember the before-and-after numbers he showed in standup, but I couldn't tell you exactly what he changed or why he ruled out other options — I wasn't involved in that part.
answers.rust_hands_on: I haven't written any Rust code, so I don't have a real story here.
answers.rust_when_not: I'd guess something that's actively changing shouldn't be rewritten in a new language, but I don't have real experience holding back a rewrite myself to back that up.
answers.reconciliation_mismatch: I haven't personally chased a reconciliation mismatch. When our numbers were off once, another engineer did the investigation and told the team the cause afterward, but I wasn't involved in finding it.
answers.prod_data_verification: I haven't been in a spot where I was tempted to check something against production data myself. If something couldn't be reproduced in staging, I'd probably ask someone more senior how to verify it safely rather than figure it out on my own.
